q: My first born was 8 months old when we sleep trained him as he was waking up 3 times a night and he started sleeping through the night right from day 1 of sleep training. I expected something similar with my 2nd one.
cx: Second baby, almost 6 months, still wakes every two hours days into the same training that worked on the first.

q: I let her cry before picking her up and nursing but it escalates and I feel like I will wake up the entire neighborhood. How long do you typically wait before giving in to nursing?
cx: Mother asks how long to wait before nursing during night wakings in sleep training.

q: Into her own room isn’t possible in our current situation. Is it ok to change up her routine mid sleep training? Im on day3 tonight.
cx: Commenters suggest moving the baby to her own room; space rules it out.

q: Yes i think I panicked thinking I might have made things worse
cx: Mother after night three of sleep training with hourly wakings.

q:
If she naps (usually around 12 for about an hour) she will not go to bed at night without such a fight (like 9/10pm). It’s exhausting fighting every night with her to sleep.

If she doesn’t nap she’ll be exhausted by 4/5pm, where she becomes the clumsiest toddler you’ve ver seen.
cx: Two-and-a-half-year-old: nap means a late bedtime fight, no nap means collapse by late afternoon.

q: I want to, but I just feel bad on her dad not seeing her after work.
cx: Replies suggest an earlier bedtime; parent hesitates because the father would miss her after work.

q: She isn’t overtired, I’ve seen her overtired and it’s not that.
cx: Parent rejects the usual overtired explanation for a toddler awake until 9 or 10pm.

q: This evening has been one of the worst trying to get him down - we both ended up crying before he fell asleep in my arms.
cx: 7-month-old waking every 2-3 hours, never one good night; mother posts in tears asking where to start.

q: I feel like a failure of a parent, I just don't know what to do. Please kind comments only, I've been balling my eyes out all evening, I don't need to feel lower than I already am.
cx: Opening of a sleep-training request from an exhausted mother pre-empting harsh replies.

q: I feel like everyone mentions CIO or Ferber, I just can't seem to see them working when he just winds himself up. I've tried getting the other half to settle him, but he only wants me.
cx: Mother doubts the standard methods for a baby who escalates when left; partner cannot settle him.

q: This evening was CIO, it was over an hour before he projectile vomited because he was so worked up. I stopped, there is no way I can let him get to that stage again. Ferber was very similar, it breaks me apart
cx: Vomiting ends a cry-it-out attempt; Ferber went the same way.

q: Thank you, it's good to hear what other EBF babies do. I just assumed he has low sleep needs and we have both been suffering.
cx: Replies suggest longer wake windows; mother had assumed her baby simply needed little sleep.

q: I work days (7-2) dad works nights (230-1030). I leave for work around 630.
cx: Shift-working parents of a 9-month-old whose naps and evenings fell apart; baby sleeps in their bed.

q: I don’t know what to do. We can’t control how much she sleeps.
cx: Naps swap length day to day; parent asks for advice or solidarity.

q: His last pediatrician appt she just said “wow, he must be very low sleep needs.”
cx: Single mother of a nearly 3-year-old awake 7am to 11pm with no naps; paediatrician's only comment.

q: I am a single mom and have literally ZERO time to myself. I am running on fumes.
cx: Toddler stops napping at two and falls asleep around 11pm.

q: I have gone as far as closing us in the bedroom with the lights off but he stays awake for hours, until 11pm. Literally nothing helps. I am so burned out and feel like this can’t be normal.
cx: No evening screens, dim lights, steady routine; the toddler still stays awake.

q: And yes, we live in a basement apartment that is pretty small so there is only one bedroom.
cx: Space limits rule out separate rooms for mother and toddler.

q: During nap time, my husband has to drive around town otherwise my son won’t sleep for naps.
cx: Working mother; stay-at-home father of a 15-month-old who only naps in the car.

q: I’m still breastfeeding my 15 month old to sleep and my husband reads to our 3.5 year old for bedtime. We stay with our children until they fall asleep. In doing so, we often end up getting very sleepy or fall asleep ourselves. And then get very behind on chores.
cx: Long bedtimes with two children swallow the parents' evenings.

q: My dad was visiting and said that it’s a choice that we’re making every day to not do chores and that it will pile up unless we make other choices.
cx: Grandfather's verdict on parents who stay with their children until they sleep.

q: It still took about 30 minutes just to get her asleep, and I’m honestly scared to even get out of bed because I’m worried she’ll wake up.
cx: Two-year-old who slept well now takes one to two hours to fall asleep and wakes 1-3am.

q: Is this a typical 2-year-old sleep regression? Could the inconsistent naps be contributing? Is she overtired, undertired, going through separation anxiety, or something else?
cx: Parent just learned daycare naps are inconsistent and cannot tell which cause applies.

q: I’m also wondering whether I’m accidentally reinforcing the nighttime waking by bringing her into our bed, but at 1–3 AM I’m honestly just desperate for everyone to get some sleep.
cx: Parent brings a waking toddler into the adult bed out of exhaustion and worries it feeds the habit.

q: I have never been able to extend naps, no matter where they take place (contact, stroller, etc) they last only 30-40 minutes.
cx: 19-week-old on four short naps; parent stuck between overtiredness and too little day sleep.

q: My baby is great with my husband all day but then the past 1-2 weeks he has started to be inconsolable with my husband at night, around 7-8pm. He will ONLY stop crying with me (mom)
cx: 5-month-old who slept well in the bassinet suddenly refuses his father at night.

q: I have been dreading nighttime. He has been waking up at night multiple times and I need to get up or else he won’t stop crying. But then I still need to get up early for work. And all of this would be fine if there were just SOME nights where I didn’t  NEED to be the one to console him.
cx: Working mother is the only one who can settle the baby at night.

q: I’m madly trying to catch up on cleaning laundry and get him a bath before his sitter gets here but I’m afraid I have accidentally trained this kid to be completely nocturnal. Any ideas to try to correct this?
cx: First-time single mother of an almost 2-month-old returns to work days after both were ill.

q:
Who would’ve known the sleep regression would be the least of my worries.   
Just feels like everything has gone backwards.
cx: Since 4 months the baby regressed in feeding, burping and carrier use as well as sleep.

q: I want to be at home with him so badly and I dreaded going back to work, but the days I am at home with him just feels like a constant struggle. I find myself wondering if he’d be better off with me back at work permanently.
cx: Part-time working mother of a 5-month-old at her wits' end.

q: I used Ferber for bedtime at 6 months. LO took to it lovely!
cx: Ferber worked at 6 months; teeth and illness brought back wakings every 2-3 hours by 8 months.

q: Then the poopy diaper hit the fan. Teeth, one after the other. Roseola. Another tooth.
cx: Mother lists the run of setbacks that undid sleep training.

q: Then last night 2 hours of yelling. It was brutal. I currently have the flu, and have been paranoid about him being sick again so I caved, picked him up and soothed him.
cx: Night five of re-training: crying had been shortening, then two hours of screaming; sick mother gives in.

q: He woke up twice more, then sometime around 1:30am as I was sitting in my room crying at the baby monitor he fell asleep on his own.
cx: Mother's night during re-sleep-training at 8 months.

q: I feel like I ruined the progress of sleep training. I can't tell if I need a schedule change or just to preserve. I was so hopeful after reading so many success stories of ferber that it would work, but I'm at a loss day 5. I'm sick, tired, and upset with myself
cx: Online success stories raised expectations that the second round of Ferber did not meet.

q: He is an EXTREMELY sensitive baby mood wise and is a “scream bloody murder” until he throws up kind of guy so crying it out is not an option.
cx: 8-month-old still nursing 3+ times a night; mother asks for a non-crying method for night wakings.

q: I have tried, admittedly not consistently, just a handful of times to try and get him to fall asleep after his first wake up without nursing hoping that maybe that would help. This ends in 45 mins+ of me holding him screaming bloody murder until he passes out in my arms exhausted, and then won’t transfer so I end up nursing him anyways.
cx: Attempts to settle without nursing end with nursing anyway.

q: he is an amazing and involved parent, and he’s tried his hardest to get up with him before to give me a break but he becomes completely inconsolable for anything but the boob.
cx: Mother about to leave the baby overnight with his father for the first time.

q: She was so frustrated with me arching and crying so i just sat her down and then she went to sleep on her own in a few minutes. Is this normal? I’m kinda sad at the idea i can’t rock her to sleep again even if she’s sick…
cx: After quick Ferber success at 5 months, the baby refuses rocking even when ill.

q: After his first bday we did travel, so I’m thinking he’s still adjusting from that as well. We live in TN and traveled to the west coast for 5 days :( I just feel so defeated and tired!
cx: 12-month-old who slept through now wakes for hours; parent also just went back to work.

q: Having a contact napper was restrictive enough but I'm now basically stuck with boob napping or car napping which gives me no freedom at all.
cx: 4-month-old who napped only in the carrier suddenly screams in it.

q: It was recommended to us at a sling library, would never have come across it otherwise which is a shame because it's really great!
cx: Both parents bought the same named sling after a sling library recommended it.

q: There are people who have had a full nights sleep giving sleep advice, whether it be on the internet or in real life, who have absolutely NO IDEA what it is like trying to do this whole keeping an infant alive thing while exhausted.
cx: Mother of one terrible and one easy sleeper warns parents about advice from people with easy babies.

q: We tried everything (YES. EVERYTHING.) he’s 3.5 years old and still doesn’t sleep through the night. Then I had my second baby, and he just…… sleeps.
cx: Same parents, same approach, opposite sleepers.

q: They might say “oh well we zip him into this very specific sleep suit, and we make sure his wake windows are just right, and we give him exactly 3.75 ounces, then lay him on this specific mattress in this specific crib, the room is at exactly 71 degrees, and then he sleeps perfectly!”
cx: Mother mocks how parents of easy sleepers credit their routine.

q: There’s a lot of people out there who have it easy and simply don’t know it. No hate to these people (I’m currently one of them!!!), but please know that they are playing a different game than you.
cx: Closing line of a widely answered post on sleep advice and temperament.

q: “Drowsy but awake” can kiss my ass. I wish I could erase this saying from the minds of all parents
cx: Reply in the thread about who gives sleep advice.

q: Parents will be like “I wake up before my kids to take some time for myself and work out or clean” and I just laugh with rage because my kids wake up by 5:30 everyday, usually closer to 5am.
cx: Mother of early risers on advice from parents whose children sleep in.
